claims.explanation: Crizotinib selectively kills cells whose survival depends on ALK or MET kinase signaling, most clearly through oncogenic ALK activation (fusion or activating mutation) and MET amplification/overexpression, while downstream PI3K-MTOR pathway mutations and KRAS/BRAF-driven lines are largely resistant. The virtual-cell signature (strong similarity to the ALK inhibitor NVP-TAE684 and PI3K pathway drugs) supports on-target ALK/MET inhibition as the selective mechanism.

features.basis: Activating ALK alterations (fusion/hotspot) are the validated crizotinib biomarker; SKNSH neuroblastoma line is ALK-mutant and selectively killed
MET is a direct crizotinib target; MET-altered HGC27 gastric line is among the most killed
ROS1 fusions are crizotinib-sensitive oncogenic drivers
KRAS-mutant lines (PATU8988T/S, NCIH1792, RKN, LS1034) are largely resistant, consistent with bypass of RTK dependence
BRAF-mutant melanoma/colorectal lines (LOXIMVI, K029AX, SNUC5, CAL12T, SH4) are mostly in the least-affected group
PIK3CA-mutant lines are enriched among least-affected (SNUC5, MKN1, HCC1954), suggesting downstream PI3K activation bypasses ALK/MET blockade
PTEN loss activates PI3K signaling downstream of ALK/MET; PTEN-mutant lines (786O, HEC265) show weak killing
NF1 loss causes RAS-MAPK activation independent of ALK/MET; NF1-mutant lines (MDAMB175VII, NCIH2052, LOXIMVI) are resistant
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines (HCC4006, KYSE70) are not selectively killed, indicating alternate RTK driver
High ALK expression/fusion correlates with crizotinib response
MET overexpression/amplification predicts crizotinib sensitivity
